blocks.prompt: 2. An investor invests Rs. 150000 at an annual compound interest rate of 6% for 8 years. Find the total amount will he get after 8 years.
blocks.explanation:
Compound interest: each year the interest is added and next year's 6% is on the bigger amount.
So the amount is multiplied by the same number 1.06 every year: the yearly amounts form a G.P.
Plan: find the multiplier, write the amount after 8 years as a G.P. term, work out \((1.06)^8\).
steps:
Given: \(P = 150000\), 6% compound interest per year, 8 years.
To find: the amount \(A\) after 8 years.
Method: Amounts at the start and after each year form a G.P. with \(r = 1.06\); after 8 years the amount is \(P r^8\).

Find the yearly multiplier
\[r = 1 + \dfrac{6}{100} = 1.06\]
Why: Growing by 6% means keeping 100% and adding 6%, that is multiplying by 1.06.

Write the amounts as a G.P.
\[150000,\ 150000(1.06),\ 150000(1.06)^2,\ \ldots\]
\[A = 150000(1.06)^8\]
Why: The first term is the amount at the start (year 0); after 8 years there are 8 factors of 1.06, so \(A = a_9 = a_1 r^8\).

Find the amount
\[A = 150000 \times 1.59384807\]
\[\approx 239077.21\]
Why: Multiply the starting amount by the 8-year factor.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The answer key prints Rs. 239077.50. The exact value of \(150000(1.06)^8\) is Rs. 239077.21; the key's figure comes from rounding \((1.06)^8\) to 1.59385 too early.
